hints: Focus on the carbonyl group in ethanal and think about which part is electron poor and what kind of attacker it will attract.
Notice that $\text{CN}^-$ is a nucleophile with a lone pair, and it attacks the slightly positive carbon of the $\text{C=O}$ bond first.
Draw the product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ and count the longest chain including the nitrile carbon to get the correct hydroxy-nitrile name.
walkthrough:
**Decide the reaction type**

Think like the $\text{CN}^-$ ion. It has a lone pair and loves positive centres, so it is a nucleophile.

In ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, oxygen pulls electrons away from carbon, leaving the carbonyl carbon $\delta+$:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{C}^{\delta+}=\text{O}^{\delta-}$$

**Follow the nucleophilic addition**

The $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the $\delta+$ carbon, the $\text{C=O}$ pi bond breaks, then $\text{H}^+$ adds to oxygen to give an OH group.

Overall addition equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Name the cyanohydrin product**

The product has an OH on carbon 2 and a nitrile group. You must include the nitrile carbon when counting.

That gives a 3-carbon chain: $\text{CH}_3$ is C1? No, nitrile carbon is C1, so $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ is 2-hydroxypropanenitrile. This matches nucleophilic addition.

options.A: Product name is correct, but the type is wrong. Electrophiles attack electron rich areas, while here $\text{CN}^-$ (a nucleophile) attacks the electron poor carbonyl carbon.
options.B: Both parts are wrong. It is not electrophilic addition, and 2-hydroxyethanenitrile would have only 2 carbons. That is the product from methanal, $\text{HCHO}$, not from ethanal.
options.C: Correct on both counts. $\text{CN}^-$ acts as a nucleophile adding to the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon, so it is nucleophilic addition. The product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ contains 3 carbons including the $\text{CN}$ carbon, so it is 2-hydroxypropanenitrile.
options.D: Reaction type is correct, but the name is wrong. Students who forget to count the nitrile carbon choose ethanenitrile. Ethanal already has 2 carbons, adding $\text{CN}$ gives 3 carbons in total.
